### Position read
Opening position. Red has advanced from (0,3) to (3,3), taking the upper-left center. It is not immediately sandwichable because neither opponent color has a matching far flank.

### Our plan
Use Yellow to reinforce or claim another center square, while developing same-color pairs that can punish opposing center entries. Prioritize immediate center threats, but verify every exposed line against both opposing turns.

### Opponent tendencies
No moves observed yet. Watch whether the opponent races into the center or builds same-color flanks along rows 3–4.

### Lessons
Captures require same-color flanks and trigger only from the landing square. A piece may safely move into an existing sandwich.

### Position read
We hold center squares (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; Blue occupies (3,4). Yellow at (4,3) cannot be immediately sandwiched because the opponent lacks a same-color far flank. Green cannot prevent Red’s available sandwich from (0,5) to (3,5): Blue (3,4) lies between Red pieces at (3,3) and the landing square.

### Our plan
Unless Green creates a higher-priority threat, play Red (0,5)->(3,5), capturing Blue at (3,4). Then contest the remaining center squares while supporting occupants with same-color flank geometry. Recheck for any immediate opponent center win or multi-capture first.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue raced directly into the center at (3,4), adjacent to our Red without same-color support, allowing a prepared sandwich. Watch for Green entering (4,4) or staging lines against our Yellow.

### Lessons
A center race should be paired with tactical flank scans. Teammate center pieces coordinate occupation but cannot serve as same-color sandwich endpoints.

### Position read
We hold (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; Blue holds (3,4). Green’s move to (2,5) blocked the direct Red descent to (3,5). Red now occupies (3,6), creating a threatened landing at (3,5) that would sandwich Blue (3,4) against Red (3,3). No current losses.

### Our plan
If Blue remains at (3,4) and (3,5) is empty on Red’s next turn, play Red (3,6)->(3,5) to capture it. Expect Green (2,5)->(3,5) as a possible block; use Yellow’s intervening move to improve center control or constrain that blocker. If Blue vacates, aim to occupy (3,4) and (4,4) while preserving both existing center pieces.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses Green to obstruct prepared Red capture lanes and Blue to race into center. Recheck Green’s mobility around columns 4-6 before assuming a sandwich remains available.

### Lessons
A threatened sandwich can force a center evacuation even when an immediate capture is blocked. Account for the opponent’s second color inserting a piece on the intended landing square.

### Position read
We occupy three center squares: Red (3,3), Yellow (4,3) and Yellow (4,4); Blue occupies the fourth at (3,4). Red at (3,6) threatens to land (3,5) and sandwich Blue against Red (3,3), but Green at (2,5) can occupy (3,5) first. Blue also sits at (4,5). No losses.

### Our plan
Center victory is one Blue removal away. If Green does not block (3,5), play Red (3,6)->(3,5) to capture Blue (3,4) and win immediately. If Green blocks there, preserve the three center occupants and look for a Red maneuver that clears or bypasses the blocker. Avoid moving any center piece unless required to prevent a capture or immediate loss.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses Green to obstruct prepared Red sandwich landings and Blue to contest the center. Expect Green (2,5)->(3,5), then watch for Blue attempts to attack the Yellow center pair.

### Lessons
Three stable center occupants create a forcing threat, but the empty capture landing must be defended against obstruction. Recheck every opponent rook lane into (3,5) and the center before committing.

### Position read
We hold Red (3,3) and Yellow (4,3),(4,4); Blue holds (3,4), Green blocks at (3,5), and Blue at (4,5) is exposed to Yellow (7,6)->(4,6). Red moved from (3,6) to (2,6), preserving all center occupants while retaining the option to return to (3,6).

### Our plan
On Yellow’s turn, capture Blue (4,5) with (7,6)->(4,6) if it remains. If Blue escapes, develop a spare Yellow without moving the three center holders. A later Red return to (3,6) captures the contiguous Green/Blue center line only if Green has not opened a gap. After clearing (3,4), we must still occupy it to win.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses Green (3,5) as a movable shield for Blue (3,4). Expect Blue to evacuate (4,5), then Green either to retain the blockade or move to break Red’s sandwich geometry.

### Lessons
Removing the opponent from a center square does not itself complete center occupation; the vacated square must be filled. Preserve the three established center pieces while creating a safe route for a spare piece into (3,4).

### Position read
We hold Red (3,3) and Yellow (4,3); Blue holds center (3,4). Blue captured our Yellow at (4,4), raising Yellow to 1 loss. Green at (3,0) threatened to land on (3,2) and capture Red (3,3) plus Blue (3,4) against Green (3,5). Yellow moved (7,1)->(3,1), blocking Green’s row-3 approach.

### Our plan
Preserve the center holders and rebuild occupation of (4,4). On Red’s next turn, if Green remains at (3,5), consider (2,6)->(3,6), which sandwiches Green (3,5) and Blue (3,4) against Red (3,3). After (3,4) is cleared, route a spare piece there while maintaining (3,3),(4,3),(4,4). Watch Blue’s vertical pair at (3,4)/(5,4), which can capture anything between them when one flank moves into place.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses mixed-color center lines tactically and exploited Blue’s same-color vertical flanks to capture Yellow (4,4). Green is likely to move (3,5) now to avoid Red’s return capture.

### Lessons
Before contesting center occupation, scan mixed lines for a same-color far flank. Blocking the mover’s landing corridor can neutralize a multi-capture without disturbing established center pieces.

### Position read
We hold Red (3,3), Yellow (3,1)/(4,3); Blue holds (3,4). Red moved (2,6)->(3,6), so (3,6)->(3,5) captures Blue (3,4) against Red (3,3) if Blue stays. Yellow has 1 loss; all others have 0.

### Our plan
Exploit the forced Blue retreat from (3,4). If Blue moves to (4,4), Yellow (7,6)->(4,6) sandwiches Blue at (4,5) and (4,4) against Yellow (4,3), a double capture. If Blue retreats vertically upward, use the freed (3,4) while preserving Red (3,3), then rebuild toward all four centers. Watch Green (2,5) potentially moving to (3,5) as a blocker.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent has defended center tactically and moved Green away from the threatened row-3 sandwich. Expect Blue to retreat to (2,4) or (1,4), avoiding both Red’s capture and Yellow’s double-capture geometry.

### Lessons
Same-color flanks can force a center holder away even without an immediate capture. Always scan the teammate’s next move: Yellow’s (4,3)/(7,6) alignment makes Blue’s apparent refuge at (4,4) dangerous.

### Position read
Yellow moved (7,5)->(4,5), sandwiching Blue (4,4) against Yellow (4,3). Blue now has 1 loss; Yellow has 1. We hold centers (3,3) Red and (4,3) Yellow; Blue still holds (3,4), while (4,4) is empty. Red (3,6) threatens to land (3,5) and capture Blue (3,4) against Red (3,3).

### Our plan
Preserve the row-3 Red flank and clear Blue from (3,4). If Green does not occupy (3,5), execute Red (3,6)->(3,5). Yellow at (4,5) is positioned to enter (4,4) later; after clearing and occupying (3,4), this creates a direct center-win route. If Green blocks (3,5), seek another Red landing that restores the sandwich rather than sacrificing central anchors.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent chose Blue (4,5)->(4,4), avoiding the predicted double capture but allowing an immediate single capture. Green (2,5)->(3,5) is the most natural defensive reply because it blocks Red’s landing square.

### Lessons
When a retreat vacates the intended landing square, check whether another same-color piece can land there immediately; Yellow (7,5) converted the altered geometry into a clean capture.

### Position read
We hold centers (3,3) Red and (4,3) Yellow; the opponent holds (3,4), and (4,4) is empty. Green blocked our planned Red landing at (3,5). Our Red at (3,6) was exposed to Blue (2,7)->(3,7), which would sandwich it and Green (3,5) against Blue (3,4), so Red withdrew to (2,6). Losses: we have Red 0, Yellow 1; opponent Blue 1, Green 0.

### Our plan
Protect the two central anchors and look for a safe way to clear Blue (3,4). Red (2,6) remains mobile near the center. Yellow (4,5) can contest (4,4), but Blue entering (4,4) between our two Yellow pieces is safe until a Yellow flank can move away and return. Avoid leaving mixed lines that let one opponent color capture several pieces.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent used Green (2,5)->(3,5) to block the immediate sandwich of Blue (3,4). Expect Blue to reinforce or relocate its central piece, especially toward (4,4), and Green to keep obstructing Red’s row-3 geometry.

### Lessons
After a capture threat is blocked, scan beyond the blocker: Blue had a counter-sandwich landing at (3,7) that made the advanced Red flank unsafe.

### Position read
We hold centers (3,3) Red and (4,3) Yellow; Blue holds (3,4) and (4,4). Losses: Red 0, Yellow 1; Blue 1, Green 0. Yellow moved (4,5)->(5,5), leaving the central anchor in place and creating a direct return-sandwich threat against Blue (4,4).

### Our plan
On the next Yellow turn, (5,5)->(4,5) captures Blue (4,4) against Yellow (4,3) if the lane remains open. Green can block (4,5) from (3,5), but then Yellow (7,6)->(4,6) threatens to capture the blocker and Blue together if Blue stays. Expect Blue to retreat from (4,4); then consolidate the vacated center and seek a safe attack on Blue (3,4). Protect Yellow, already at 1 loss.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses Green to obstruct same-color sandwich landings and Blue to reinforce the center. Expect Green (3,5)->(4,5) or another interference, followed by Blue evacuating (4,4).

### Lessons
A supported return-square threat can force a central retreat without vacating our own center anchor. Check whether a blocker creates an alternate multi-capture lane.

### Position read
Red (2,6)->(2,5) captures Green (1,5) against Red (0,5), making losses Red 0, Yellow 1, Blue 1, Green 1. We still hold centers (3,3) Red and (4,3) Yellow; Blue holds (3,4) and (4,4).

### Our plan
Blue's center is forked. Yellow (5,5)->(4,5) sandwiches Blue (4,4) against Yellow (4,3). If Blue saves that piece, Red (2,5)->(3,5) next turn sandwiches Blue (3,4) against Red (3,3). If Blue saves (3,4), execute the Yellow capture. Recheck Green's intervening move for any new blocker or counter-capture, but no current Green piece appears able to reach either landing square immediately.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent had used Green to obstruct center capture lanes, but moved the key blocker from (3,5) to (1,5), where it was capturable. Expect Blue to evacuate one center piece and Green to seek interference with the remaining threat.

### Lessons
Coordinate same-color flanks across both rows: simultaneous Red and Yellow sandwich threats can overload the opponent's single Blue turn.

### Position read
Yellow (7,6)->(6,6) blocks Blue (6,7) from reaching (6,5), preventing a sandwich of Yellow (5,5) against Blue (4,5). Losses remain Red 0, Yellow 1, Blue 1, Green 1. Centers: Red (3,3), Blue (3,4), Yellow (4,3), with (4,4) empty.

### Our plan
After the opponent's Green turn, Red (2,5)->(3,5) should sandwich Blue (3,4) against Red (3,3), raising Blue to 2 losses. If Blue then moves (4,5)->(4,4), Yellow (5,5)->(4,5) captures it against Yellow (4,3), eliminating Blue. If Blue evacuates elsewhere, use the cleared center and keep Yellow (5,5) safe.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue retreats endangered center pieces and may use edge pieces for remote sandwich landings. Green may try to obstruct Red's landing square, though no current Green has a direct route to (3,5).

### Lessons
Check distant rook landings before preserving a tactical piece: blocking Blue's (6,7)->(6,5) route keeps the Yellow center-capture mechanism intact.

### Position read
Red (2,5)->(3,5) sandwiches Blue (3,4) against Red (3,3), raising Blue from 1 to 2 losses. Losses after capture: Red 0, Yellow 1, Blue 2, Green 1. Centers become Red (3,3), Yellow (4,3), while (3,4) and (4,4) are empty. Green recently moved to (1,4).

### Our plan
Blue is one loss from elimination. Watch especially for Blue (4,5)->(4,4): Yellow (5,5)->(4,5) would sandwich it against Yellow (4,3) and eliminate Blue. Otherwise preserve Yellow (5,5), seek another same-color flank on any Blue piece, and occupy the cleared center when tactically safe.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue retreats endangered center pieces and uses distant rook landings to create sandwiches. Green may obstruct capture lanes or pressure exposed Red pieces; its new (1,4) piece has central access.

### Lessons
Prepared same-color flanks convert center control into elimination pressure. Recheck all remote rook replies before committing the Yellow capture piece.

### Position read
Yellow moved (4,3)->(4,4). We hold centers (3,3) with Red and (4,4) with Yellow; the other two centers are empty. Losses: we have Red 0, Yellow 1; opponent has Blue 2, Green 1. Blue (4,5) is now between Yellow (4,4) and the open landing square (4,6).

### Our plan
Threaten Yellow (6,6)->(4,6), which would sandwich Blue (4,5) and eliminate Blue. Green cannot readily occupy (4,6), so Blue will likely have to retreat on its next turn. Preserve Yellow (4,4) and then exploit whichever center or lane Blue concedes. Continue targeting any Blue piece for the decisive third loss.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue has repeatedly retreated threatened pieces and may move (4,5) rightward if its vertical exits remain blocked by Red (3,5) and Yellow (5,5). Green may enter (3,4) or (4,3) to contest the center or complicate our supporting lines.

### Lessons
A safe stationary same-color flank can force a nearly eliminated color to spend its turn retreating. Verify that the intended landing square remains open and that the staging piece cannot be sandwiched first.

### Position read
We now hold centers (4,3) with Red and (4,4) with Yellow; Green occupies (3,4), while (3,3) is open. Losses: Red 0, Yellow 1; Blue 2, Green 1. Blue (4,5) remains nearly trapped, with only (4,6) or (4,7) available unless the position changes.

### Our plan
On Yellow’s next turn, strongly consider (3,1)->(3,3), giving us three center squares and blocking Green (3,4) from moving left. If Green later vacates (3,4), Red (3,5)->(3,4) wins immediately, so the opponent must keep contesting or disturb our center. If Blue leaves (4,5), preserve the Yellow (6,6) attacker and seek another same-color flank against Blue’s remaining pieces.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue retreats pieces facing a third-loss capture and will likely move (4,5) rightward. Green may keep (3,4) planted while using an edge piece to attack our support or create blocking geometry.

### Lessons
Center occupation can force a defender to remain fixed even without an immediate same-color sandwich. Recheck whether Blue’s move creates a capture or forces Yellow to defend before committing (3,1)->(3,3).

### Position read
We hold centers (4,3) with Red and (4,4) with Yellow. Yellow now also occupies (5,4), blocking the immediate Green (5,0)->(5,4) sandwich against our center Yellow. Losses: Red 0, Yellow 1; Blue 2, Green 1. Green (3,4) is threatened by Red (4,3)->(3,3), using Red (3,5) as the far flank.

### Our plan
Exploit Green’s forced response to the threatened center piece. If Green vacates (3,4), work toward filling (3,3) and (3,4) while preserving both occupied lower centers. Keep pressure on Blue, which is one capture from elimination, especially the clustered pieces at (4,6)-(4,7) and edge piece (6,7).

### Opponent tendencies
Blue retreated from (4,5) to (4,6) to avoid immediate danger. Green must now save or tactically exploit (3,4), likely by moving it upward or disturbing Red’s flank at (3,5).

### Lessons
Before advancing into a center square, scan existing same-color enemy flanks: Yellow (4,4) was vulnerable between Green (3,4) and the landing square (5,4). Occupying the attacker’s required landing square can preserve center control without retreating.

### Position read
We hold three centers: Red at (3,3),(4,3) and Yellow at (4,4). Losses: Red 0, Yellow 2; Blue 2, Green 1. Blue must prevent Red (0,4)->(3,4) from completing center; its apparent direct defense is Blue (3,7)->(3,4).

### Our plan
If Blue blocks at (3,4), preserve Red (3,3), then threaten Red (0,5)->(3,5), sandwiching that Blue against (3,3) for Blue’s third loss. On Yellow’s intervening turn, prioritize avoiding any third Yellow loss and support the trap. If Blue fails to occupy (3,4) and the square remains open, complete center with Red (0,4)->(3,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent responds to direct capture and center threats by retreating or interposing. Green recently used the (3,0)/(3,2) flank to capture Yellow at (3,1), putting Yellow at critical loss count 2.

### Lessons
At loss 2, every Yellow exposure is elimination-critical. Preserve occupied lower centers while introducing new pieces into upper centers; do not fill an upper center by vacating a lower one.

### Position read
We hold centers (3,3) Red, (4,3) Red, and (4,4) Yellow. Blue at (3,4) has 2 losses and is trapped between Red (3,3) and the available landing square (3,5). Yellow remains elimination-critical at 2 losses; the rear Yellow shifted safely to (7,3).

### Our plan
After Green moves, play Red (0,5)->(3,5) if still legal: it sandwiches Blue (3,4) against Red (3,3), causing Blue’s third loss and conversion to Void. Then preserve the three occupied centers and aim for Red (0,4)->(3,4) to complete center occupation. Keep Yellow (5,4) in place because it blocks Green access up column 4.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent interposes against center threats and uses same-color edge flanks for captures. Green’s useful pieces are concentrated on the left and currently cannot reach (3,5) or create an immediate capture of our center formation.

### Lessons
At 2 losses, move peripheral Yellow pieces without opening Green approach lanes. Same-color sandwich geometry is decisive: Red (3,3) must survive until Red lands at (3,5).

### Position read
Red (0,5)->(3,5) captures Blue at (3,4) against Red (3,3), giving Blue its third loss and converting its remaining pieces to Void. We retain centers (3,3) Red, (4,3) Red, and (4,4) Yellow; (3,4) is now the sole empty center. Yellow is still elimination-critical at 2 losses.

### Our plan
Protect the three occupied centers through the intervening Void-Blue, Yellow, and Green turns. If (3,4) remains empty and safely reachable, complete center occupation with Red (0,4)->(3,4) on our next Red turn. Keep Yellow (5,4) unless a forced defense is needed, since it restricts Green’s column-4 access.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent has used interpositions against center threats and same-color edge-flank geometry. Blue is now Void and cannot capture, so Green is the only remaining capturing color and must disrupt the center before our next Red move.

### Lessons
At 2 losses, prioritize Yellow survival and avoid exposing multiple Yellow pieces to one Green sandwich. Void turns can reposition blockers but cannot capture; check whether Blue blocks Red’s route to (3,4).

### Position read
Blue is eliminated and its Void move placed b at (3,6). We hold three centers: Red at (3,3),(4,3), Yellow at (4,4); (3,4) remains empty. Yellow has 2 losses and must avoid capture. Yellow moved (6,6)->(4,6), safely improving central support.

### Our plan
Green has the only intervening turn before Red. If (3,4) remains empty and Red’s column-4 path remains clear, play Red (0,4)->(3,4) for immediate center occupation victory. Recheck only whether Green has occupied (1,4), (2,4), or (3,4), or captured/displaced one of our three center pieces.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses interpositions and flank geometry, but Blue is Void and cannot capture. Current Green pieces cannot immediately reach (3,4), and Green at (4,2) is blocked from attacking across row 4 by our Red and Yellow center pieces.

### Lessons
Moving into a sandwich is safe, but leaving Yellow exposed at 2 losses is not. Preserve the center trio and prioritize the immediate fourth-center move over incidental captures.

### Position read
We occupy all four central squares after Red moves (0,4)->(3,4), completing an immediate center-occupation victory.

### Our plan
The game is won by center occupation.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent’s final Green move did not disrupt our center trio or block Red’s column-4 route.

### Lessons
When three centers are secured and the fourth has a clear rook path, take the immediate win before considering captures or positional improvements.
